summary: The agent ran the hyperpowers SDD skill through all six tasks in one turn (about 35 minutes). Each task got an implementer and a reviewer subagent. It waited out both soak tests (about 4 and 12 minutes) without stopping, ran the final whole-branch review plus a fix and re-review round, and ran `sdd-state finish`, which published a receipt. It stopped once, to ask merge/PR/keep. I answered "merge back to main locally" and it fast-forwarded main to 404d696. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria are met, based on the session log, git history and file hashes. There was one mid-plan stop: the finishing-menu question, which is allowed under the script. The turn stayed alive through both slow soak runs: the screen showed a spinner the whole time, and the agent ran the long soak as a tracked job.

observations.description: The startup trust dialog and the bypass-permissions warning both have 'No, exit' selected by default. A tester pressing Enter would quit Claude Code.

Claude Code was launched with `--model claude-opus-5-5`, but at startup it still said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' and offered to restart to upgrade. I chose No. The header then showed Opus 5.5, so the flag did apply, but the prompt contradicts it.

The skill asked a setup question about moving design.md into docs/ so decision records would work. The plan didn't call for that. I answered 'go ahead with what the plan says', so design.md stayed put and no decision records were created.

Per the agent's own summary, two commit subjects (fb15f9f, 66e2319) have the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5' trailer run into the subject line. The implementer subagent formatted these commits wrongly.
No .gitignore was created, so ratelimit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ are untracked in main after the merge.
`git branch -a` after the run shows a leftover `+ hyperpowers/state` branch, apparently checked out in another worktree. It's state plumbing that remains in the user's repo after finishing.

The final review found a real bug in the plan's code: float drift in simulate with --window a multiple of 0.1 gave allowed=48/denied=52 instead of 50/50. The agent fixed it with exact fractions and also added NaN/inf rejection, which the plan doesn't define. That goes beyond 'implement the plan exactly'; worth a reviewer's look.
The agent chose an in-place branch (`ratelimit`) rather than a worktree when told 'use whatever the skill recommends', so the closing summary said there was no worktree to clean up.
Codex reviews were skipped because the Codex plugin isn't installed, so every review came from Claude. The agent disclosed this.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log a8d0478b...jsonl is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`. The screen showed `Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill` before any Agent dispatch.

criteria.criterion: Every task completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on the main checkout
criteria.evidence: The log has `sdd-state complete plan.md 1..6`, then `Agent: Final whole-branch code review`, then `Agent: Fix final-review findings wave` and `Re-review final fix wave`, then `sdd-state finish plan.md`. `git log` on main shows 404d696 down to fb15f9f on top of 1199cab, with `* main` checked out. The screen said 'I merged ratelimit into main locally... moved straight to the branch tip, 404d696. All 29 unit tests pass'.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: shasum before and after is identical: long 5cd08cd9…, short 5b4fdfd0…. `git log -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returns only `1199cab initial`.

STOP: "Which option?" | question. This was the finishing menu (merge/PR/keep), shown after `sdd-state finish` had published its receipt but before the merge. I answered 'merge back to main locally'. The setup questions (workspace, DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS, spec path) came in a single AskUserQuestion form before any implementation started. I answered them as scripted. No 'continue' was ever needed.
